title: private-deploy field notes - 2026-03-06
content:
Quick field notes from calls + lab testing today (scratchpad). Purpose: capture install steps we used for Customer X (on-prem VPC), blockers seen, and short-term TODOs for next visit. Keep as informal — will clean up into runbook later.

Context:
- Customer: FinCore (regulated finance customer)
- Environment: on-prem private deployment in customer-controlled VPC, 4x A100s, dedicated subnet, restricted egress, customer KMS (vault) for keys
- Objective: get base Redwood Private runtime + model bundle deployed, validate routing to customer internal app, confirm KMS integration and audit logging.

What we actually did (high level):
1) Initial infra check (Samira + Riley)
   - Confirmed access to bastion host (jump.box.fincore.local) — used my admin cert.
   - Verified VPC subnet CIDR and security groups: infra-team created sg-redwood-internal allowing 22, 443, 50051 from internal CIDR, and 8200 for Vault. Note: customer has iptables rules that block ESTABLISHED incoming on 443 — caused initial probe fail.

2) KMS / secrets (Noah)
   - Ran integration test with Vault (KV v2). Created role "redwood-deploy" with policy to read /prod/redwood/* — OK.
   - Problem: Vault mounted at non-standard path (/secrets/v1) — our default env expects /v1/secret. Had to set REDWOOD_VAULT_PATH=/secrets/v1 in deployment env.

3) Install steps executed (notes for runbook):
   - On bastion: git clone github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-scripts, checkout tag v1.4.
   - Run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh --env prod --region local 
       * bootstrap does: create k8s namespace redwood, deploy secrets manifest (reads from Vault), apply node affinity taints for GPU nodes.
   - k8s cluster: kubelet version 1.27 (ok), RBAC: ensured clusterrolebinding redwood-admin -> serviceaccount:redwood:deployer.
   - Helm release: redwood-runtime v2.3.1 with values-overrides.yaml (attached in linked artifacts). Key overrides we used:
       * enableKvCache: true
       * quantProfile: fp16-approx
       * vault.path: /secrets/v1
       * metrics.pushGateway: "pushgateway.fincore.local:9091"

4) Smoke validation:
   - hit /health on runtime service from operator pod: 200 after ~45s.
   - ran small inference request via curl to internal API gateway at 10.10.12.8:8080/api/v1/generate — returned tokens but saw occasional 500s.
   - logs show OOMKills on model-worker-2 (pod scheduling was packing 4 workers on single GPU). Need to adjust pod resourceRequests/limits.

Blockers & strange behaviors:
- iptables rule as noted above blocked some TLS handshakes from operator -> gateway. Customer networking says rule required for legacy app; workaround: create exception for operator IP range (10.10.0.0/16). Action: ask infra team to open exception (ticket JIRA-PI-4321).
- Vault path mismatch (fixed by env override) — need to make vault path configurable in bootstrap and documented.
- OOMs on model-worker: currently resourceRequests: cpu=2000m, mem=16Gi, but actual usage peaked at ~40Gi for large model. Quick fix: bump mem to 64Gi for heavy workers and set max_workers_per_gpu=2. Longer-term: implement node-level GPU isolation policy.
- Audit logging: customer requires immutable audit logs (syslog shipped to SIEM). Our fluentd config defaulted to ephemeral logs. Action: configure fluentd persistent buffer + set output to syslog:514 with TLS. Ticket: github:infra/setup-scripts#42

Short TODOs (next 48h):
- [ ] Patch bootstrap to read REDWOOD_VAULT_PATH from env or values file (Samira)
- [ ] Add network exception request to infra (Riley) — include affected operator IPs + port list (22,443,8200,50051,8080)
- [ ] Adjust Helm values for resourceRequests/memory and max_workers_per_gpu, run canary (Noah)
- [ ] Add persistent buffer to fluentd config and test delivery to customer's SIEM (Samira + security)
- [ ] Draft one-page runbook snippet with the non-standard customer quirks (vault path, iptables exception, SIEM endpoint) and attach to Confluence (owner: Samira)

Notes for next on-site:
- Bring USB with prepared CA certs (customer uses internal CA, certs expire 2026-04-01)
- Ask customer to provide iptables audit log (they said they'd export) — will help confirm race condition where established TLS reset occurs after 2 minutes.
- Confirm model bundle checksum before starting heavy load test — last time we saw silent corruption when rsync over restrictive firewall. Use sha256sum and compare to our signed manifest.

Scratch quick commands used (copy-paste):
- clone + checkout: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/private-deploy-scripts.git && cd private-deploy-scripts && git checkout v1.4
- bootstrap: REDWOOD_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.fincore.local:8200 REDWOOD_VAULT_PATH=/secrets/v1 ./scripts/bootstrap.sh --env prod --region local
- helm upgrade: helm upgrade --install redwood-runtime ./charts/runtime -f values-overrides.yaml --namespace redwood
- tail logs: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=model-worker -f --tail=200

Questions / unresolved:
- Why did kube-scheduler pack 4 model-workers on one GPU node despite nodeSelector? Check taints/affinity rules (possible race during bootstrap).
- Does customer have any egress inspection appliance that mutates TLS and could be causing the ESTABLISHED reset? They mentioned an L7 proxy in front of internal apps. Need network diagram.

References & attachments to create:
- Confluence runbook page draft link: confluence:private-deploy-runbook (will update)
- Attach values-overrides.yaml + observed logs snippet to ticket JIRA-PI-4321

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into runbook and link artifacts tomorrow.

-- Samira
